title: Navi — model calls
description: Is the escalation ladder's tier-1 model actually adequate, or is every turn paying for a tier-2 call? L6's whole point is that this becomes a query instead of a guess after two weeks of real use, and the routing table (docs/06-agent-spec.md#model-routing) gets rewritten from what this dashboard shows, not from instinct.

panels.title: Tier-1 success rate — crud
panels.description: Share of tier-1 crud calls (the conversational agent's own task) that got a usable response from the provider, over the visible time range. A call here counts as a success purely at the model.Client.Complete level - the HTTP round trip returned a real completion, not a timeout, rate limit, or malformed body. It does not by itself mean the tool call that came back passed Layer 2/3 validation; a low number means the provider is the bottleneck, a healthy number here with a lot of tier-2 traffic on the ladder-exhaustion side means validation is the bottleneck instead.

panels.title: Tier-1 success rate by task
panels.description: The same ratio as the stat panel, per task, tracked over time rather than as a single number. A task whose line sits well below the others is the one whose tier-1 model, prompt, or tool schema is worth revisiting first.

panels.title: Calls by task, tier, outcome (visible range)
panels.description: Raw counts behind the ratios above. outcome="success" is a completion the provider returned; every other value is a model.ErrorKind (timeout, malformed, unavailable, rate_limited, empty, config) - see internal/model/error.go. A task with all its volume on tier 2 is a tier-1 model that is effectively never used.

panels.title: Copywriter generations by pass and outcome
panels.description: Generation attempts that ran to an outcome, per hour. generated is text stored ahead of the reminder; failed is the model erroring or its text being refused (empty, over 120 characters, a repeat of a recent message); late is text that arrived after the scheduler had already claimed the row and was discarded by the guarded write. Pass 2 only runs when the context changed since pass 1, so it should sit well under pass 1. Items below the history threshold (G9) make no attempt and are not here - they are plain titles by design.

panels.title: Plain titles after a failed generation (6h)
panels.description: Reminders that went out as the bare title because the copywriter had tried and failed (navi_copywriter_fallback_total). Zero is the healthy value; a rising number is the model provider failing while reminders still arrive. Items below G9's history threshold and deployments with no model are plain by design and are not counted - the fire-path dashboard has the share of all deliveries.
